1.title: The Seven Principles and Tailoring
1.text: Welcome to Module two: The Seven Principles and Tailoring. It covers the exam area The prince two principles. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. Explain the seven principles. Explain how and why the principles provide the basis for applying prince two, which factors influence how the method is tailored, who is responsible and how tailoring decisions are documented. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: The prince two principles (eight percent). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: The seven principles
1.text: The seven principles. The principles are the guiding obligations and good practices that determine whether a project is really being managed with prince two. If a principle is not applied, the project is not using prince two.

1.title: The seven principles, continued
1.text: The seven principles. The figure shows this: The seven prince two principles.

1.title: The seven principles, continued
1.text: The seven principles. one. Principle: Ensure continued business justification. In one line: There is a documented reason for the project that stays valid all the way. two. Principle: Learn from experience. In one line: Seek, record and apply lessons throughout. three. Principle: Define roles, responsibilities and relationships. In one line: Everyone knows who does what and who they work with. four. Principle: Manage by stages. In one line: Plan, monitor and control the project stage by stage.

1.title: The seven principles, continued
1.text: The seven principles. five. Principle: Manage by exception. In one line: Set tolerances; escalate only when they would be exceeded. six. Principle: Focus on products. In one line: Concentrate on what is delivered and its quality, not just on activity. seven. Principle: Tailor to suit the project. In one line: Adapt prince two to the project's context. Exam tip: Learn the seven names in this order. Scenario questions describe a behavior and ask which principle it shows or breaks.

1.title: What each principle means in practice
1.text: What each principle means in practice. Continued business justification. A business case exists, is approved, and is checked at every decision point; the project stops if it is no longer justified. Learn from experience. Review past lessons at the start, record new ones in the lessons log, and share them at the end. Roles, responsibilities, relationships. A project management team structure covers the business, user and supplier interests. Manage by stages. The project has at least two management stages (initiation and one more); the board authorizes each stage.

1.title: What each principle means in practice, continued
1.text: What each principle means in practice. Manage by exception. Authority is delegated within tolerances; an exception goes up to the next level. Focus on products. Product descriptions with quality criteria are agreed before work starts. Tailor. Adapt the method, documenting the decision, but keep the principles.

1.title: Tailoring
1.text: Tailoring. Tailoring means adapting prince two so it fits the project's size, complexity, importance, team capability, risk and environment, without losing its principles. Processes can be simplified or carried out in more detail. The principles. Terminology can be changed to match organizational standards. The intent of each practice (each must be addressed). Practices are adapted to the project. The need for the project board to remain accountable. Roles can be combined in sensible ways. A business case and control by the board.

1.title: Tailoring, continued
1.text: Tailoring. Some roles can be combined, but not all combinations are allowed: for example, the person who manages the project should not also provide project assurance of their own work. Who is responsible, and where is it recorded: the project manager is responsible for tailoring the method to the project, and tailoring decisions are documented in the project initiation documentation (P I D), which the project board approves. Exam tip: Tailoring never means leaving out a principle. An option that says a practice can be ignored completely or that any combination of roles is allowed is wrong. Exam tip: Scenario questions describe a behavior (no stage approval, no business case review, no product definition). Name the principle that behavior breaks.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A project board approves the business case, then never looks at it again until the end. Which principle is being broken? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Ensure continued business justification. The justification must be checked and remain valid throughout.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A project manager asks the board to approve a plan for the next stage before the stage begins. Which principle does this support? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Manage by stages. The board authorizes work stage by stage.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statements about tailoring are C O R R E C T? (one) Processes can be simplified or carried out in more detail. (two) Terminology can be changed to match organizational standards. (three) A principle can be left out if the project is small. (four) Project team members can combine any roles at all. The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: one and two. Processes and terminology can be tailored; principles are not dropped and not every role combination is allowed.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Identify the missing word. The principle "manage by blank" delegates authority within agreed tolerances. The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Exception. Manage by exception uses tolerances and escalation.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team writes a product description with quality criteria before building the product. Which principle does this show? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Focus on products. Defining the product and its quality first is a product focus.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Where are tailoring decisions documented? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: In the P I D. Tailoring decisions are documented in the P I D.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the seven principles. Answer: Ensure continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project. Question two. What is the minimum number of management stages? Answer: Two (the initiation stage and at least one more). Question three. What does manage by exception use? Answer: Tolerances, with escalation when they would be exceeded.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is tailoring? Answer: Adapting prince two to fit the project's context without losing the principles. Question five. Who is responsible for tailoring? Answer: The project manager (the project board approves the P I D that records it). Question six. If a principle is not applied, what does that mean? Answer: The project is not being managed using prince two.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Principles: business justification, learn from experience, roles, stages, exception, products, tailor. Stages: at least two. Exception: tolerances and escalation. Tailoring: adapt, document in the P I D, never drop principles.
